chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'O Muhammad! Indeed your Lord conveys greetings to you and forbids the decoration of houses.' Abu Baseer said, 'So I said, 'What is the decoration of the houses?' He said, 'The images of statues.'

key_terms.تَزْوِيق: Decoration or adorning (specifically with images/statues in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific meaning of 'decoration of houses' (tazweeq) forbidden in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Angel Jibril conveys Allah's command to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) to prohibit 'tazweeq' (decoration) in homes, which Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies specifically as the creation or display of images of statues (*tasawwir al-tamathil*). This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between permissible decorative patterns and the prohibited depiction of animate beings, reflecting the theological emphasis on avoiding idolatrous associations in domestic spaces. The clarification by Abu Basir highlights the precise scope of the prohibition, linking it directly to the preservation of monotheism within the household.
